subject: Request: Retroactive early-commitment credit for Orion Health POC
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@orionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: POC usage overage — request for credit

Aditya,

Thanks again for the tight timeline on the POC last month — the team at Orion has been impressed with the latency profile and the rollout notes. We ran into an unexpectedly high token volume during the last two weeks of testing (spike from synthetic load), which put us beyond the quoted usage for the free trial.

Can Redwood consider a retroactive credit (or one-off invoice adjustment) for the POC so our finance team can approve the platform for the production procurement review? If possible, wed like the credit to be documented in writing so procurement can close internal approvals.

Happy to share logs / sample queries if that helps.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior PM, Integrations
Orion Health
liam.oconnor@orionhealth.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC usage overage — request for credit

Team — forwarding a brief from Orion (see below). TL;DR: they exceeded their POC allocation (synthetic load during integration), are asking for a retroactive credit against the one-month invoice so procurement will sign the production SOW.

Key numbers (attached usage report):
- Total billed tokens for POC window: ~$32,400
- Expected trial cap: $10,000
- Proposed one-off credit requested by customer: $22,000

My recommendation: offer a compromise — a retro credit equal to the lesser of (a) 30% of the overage or (b) $25k, contingent on a 12-month production commitment and a signed commercial addendum capturing usage SLAs. This preserves economics while giving procurement a documented concession.

Attachments: orion_poc_usage_report.csv, proposed_credit_term_sheet.xlsx

Asking @Marissa: need VP/CFO level signoff for any credit > $10k. If you can OK the framing above, Ill confirm with Orion and route the updated term sheet to procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Healthcare
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC usage overage — request for credit

Aditya — thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before routing to finance:

- Was the synthetic load tied to an integration partner or test harness we can point to in the concession language? (procurement likes concrete cause statements)
- Is the 12-month production commitment a firm MRR or a usage-based commit?
- Can we require the credit to be applied only after the first full production invoice (i.e., not reduce the POC invoice but provide a production credit)?

If we make the credit contingent on a signed 12-month commitment with a 2x minimum monthly spend guarantee, Id be comfortable pushing up to $25k. Anything above that would need Marissa/finance OK.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Enterprise Sales — East
Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC usage overage — request for credit

Thanks for the context. Ive reviewed the numbers and the proposed conditions. I approve a retroactive credit structure as follows:

- Credit: up to $22,000 applied as a credit against the customers first two production invoices (split evenly), provided the customer executes the 12-month commitment addendum within 14 days.
- Commit requirement: 12 months with a monthly minimum equal to twice their observed average monthly usage during the POC window.
- Documentation: Legal to prepare a one-page addendum that references the POC dates, attaches the usage report, and specifies the credit schedule and clawback if they churn in the first 180 days.
- Approval limit: this disposition is final from Revenue leadership; Finance to sign off on the accounting treatment for the credit.

Aditya — please confirm youll (a) update the term sheet with these conditions, (b) get an explicit procurement email acknowledging the schedule, and (c) loop Legal. I dont want to set a precedent without the 180-day clawback.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (650) 555-0147
